The joke hinges on a pun: in school being a “good student” often means that you “pass” your classes. A judge “passes” sentences, but a cashier “makes change” rather than “passing” anything. Thus, in the riddle the judge is playfully implied to have “passed” while the cashier didn’t, making the cashier the “bad student.”

The passage tells us that parents of both affluent and working‐class students are invited to attend parent–teacher conferences. In other words, it is not just the affluent parents or just the working‐class parents who show care—both groups are encouraged (and so implied to be attentive) when it comes to their children's schooling.

None of the options lists “both” as a single choice, but since the only two groups mentioned that are encouraged to be involved are the affluent and the working‐class, the best answer is that both groups are attentive.

Since “both” is not given, the most accurate answer is to note that both (0) and (2) are correct.
